key_insight: SLiR turns activation-function relaxation into a general, shift-based optimization problem that can soundly handle many nonlinearities without custom manual derivations.
engineering_relevance: This makes neural network verification easier to extend to modern activation functions while preserving tight, optimizable bounds needed for safety-critical systems.
method: Parameterize each linear relaxation by its slope.
Compute the intercept via a shifting procedure that enforces sound upper and lower bounds over the input domain.
Use either a Lipschitz constant or a set of critical points as the only function-specific input.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that SLiR achieves tight relaxations across many practical activations and verifies up to 7.8x more properties than state-of-the-art methods.
watch_item: Soundness and tightness still depend on correctly identifying the Lipschitz bound or critical points, so poor estimates could weaken the relaxation.
paper_title: Shifting-based Optimizable Linear Relaxations for General Activation Functions
